name: FEVER
description: Fact Extraction and VERification (FEVER) is a benchmark for fact verification against textual sources. Models are given claims and must classify them as Supported, Refuted, or NotEnoughInfo using Wikipedia, and also identify the evidence sentences. Claims were generated by mutating sentences from Wikipedia and were then verified by crowdworkers.
evaluation_method: FEVER score (label accuracy conditioned on correct evidence retrieval) and label accuracy
reputation: Foundational fact verification benchmark; drove research in claim verification, evidence retrieval, and misinformation detection; introduced the FEVER shared task
notes: Introduced at NAACL 2018. Contains 185,445 claims; 80% supported or refuted, 20% not enough info. Led to FEVER 2.0 and Fever-Symmetric. Claims span diverse topics across 50K Wikipedia articles. Shared tasks in 2018 and 2019 drove progress. Important for research in automated fact-checking and misinformation detection.
